nodes.text: kinda had absolutely no idea where to go from here; decided to ask claude. it made a VERY important point - all PNG images start with the same 8-byte header. that gives us an anchor for our input
30 minutes in now
i still wasn't fully good on what this script is actually doing. after some time, here's what i've determined:

subNodes.text: basically, imagine the flat bytes array as a table with 16 columns (len) and 44 rows (704 total bytes / len)
it's gonna read in each row column-by-column. for each column, in each iteration R, it will read the row at (R + shifter) % number of rows
if we're at row R=0, and let's say our shifter is 3, that becomes it's reading row [3 % 44] = row 3.
at row R=1, shifter 3, it's gonna read row [4 % 44] = row 4
at row R=42, shifter 3, it's gonna read row [45 % 44] = row 1
so essentially, we're rotating the entire column by that shifter value, and each of the 16 cols have their own shifter, equal to whatever the character in the input is at that position

nodes.text: this is cool - basically we can enum character-by-character. problem is, while the first 8 bytes are always the same on PNGs, the next 8 might not be. lemme see if theres some sort of pattern we can abuse there too

subNodes.text: ayy, ok so theres more PNG structure stuff in the next 16B - it doesnt HAVE to be this way, but that first chunk (length and chunk type) is likely gonna be the IHDR chunk which is always 13B long

this being Java Script Kiddie 1, the FIRST challenge in this series, i think we can safely assume the next 4 bytes are gonna be 00 00 00 0D (for length, 13) and then the hex codes for IHDR so 49 48 44 52.
